newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CLARK PITCHES SEVEN NO-HIT INNINGS AND HOMERS FOR METS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLARK PITCHES SEVEN NO-HIT INNINGS AND HOMERS FOR METS.

text.p: Mark Clark took a no-hitter into the eighth inning and hit his first major league home run to lead the New York Mets to a 5-2 victory over the Boston Red Sox in interleague play on Saturday.

Clark lost a bid at the first no-hitter in Mets history when pinch-hitter Reggie Jefferson singled to left field to lead off the eighth. He then gave up a double to Nomar Garciaparra and was taken out of the game.

Clark (6-4) was charged with two runs on two hits with five walks, but helped his own cause by sparking a three-run fifth inning with a homer off Tim Wakefield (2-6) for his first hit since last August.
"It got to be real exciting in the sixth and seventh," Clark said of his no-hit bid. "I kept telling myself, 'Don't look at the scoreboard.'"

An error by second baseman Carlos Baerga and three walks helped Boston score a run without a hit in the sixth to pull within 4-1. Mets catcher Todd Hundley scored an insurance run in the eighth on a wild pitch by Boston reliever Joe Hudson.

In Atlanta, Chris Hoiles, who struck out in his first five at-bats, delivered a two-run double in the top of the 12th to lift the Baltimore Orioles a 6-4 victory over the Atlanta Braves in a potential World Series preview.

Cal Ripken and Tony Tarasco drew walks off reliever Joe Borowski (2-2) before Hoiles followed with a double to right field, scoring both runners. "It didn't start off very good," Hoiles said, "but it sure ended very good."
Arthur Rhodes (4-2) struck out six over three hitless innings to earn the victory.

In Montreal, the Expos extended their winning streak to eight as Pedro Martinez recorded a career-high 14 strikeouts in a three-hit complete-game shutout to outduel Justin Thompson for a 1-0 victory over the Detroit Tigers.
Martinez (9-2) has at least 12 strikeouts in each of his last three outings. Thompson (6-5) struck out seven in seven innings, giving up five hits and three walks.
The Expos got the only run in the fourth when Mike Lansing doubled and scored on Rondell White's sacrifice fly.
In Philadelphia, Joe Carter's two-run homer snapped a seventh-inning tie and Orlando Merced doubled in a run and scored as the Toronto Blue Jays edged the Phillies 3-2.

Carter, whose ninth-inning homer in Game 6 of the 1993 World Series clinched Toronto's victory over the Phillies, drove an 0-2 pitch from starter Ryan Nye (0-2) over the left-field wall to score Merced and give Toronto a 3-1 lead.
Robert Person (2-4) gave us two runs and seven hits in 6-2/3 innings for the win.
In Pittsburgh, Jeff King homered twice against his former team and drove in three runs to power the Kansas City Royals to an 8-3 victory over the Pirates.
King hit a solo shot in the eighth to make it 6-3 and cleared the wall with a runner on in the ninth for the final margin. Sal Fasano also homered for the Royals.
Tim Belcher (8-6) allowed three runs and seven hits -- all singles -- in seven innings to pick up the win. Pittsburgh's Jon Lieber (3-8) allowed five runs in taking the loss.
In Cincinnati, Kent Mercker allowed four hits in eight shutout innings and Willie Greene hit a solo homer to lead the Reds to their sixth win in seven games, a 5-1 victory over the Chicago White Sox.
Deion Sanders collected his 500th major-league hit, an RBI single in the first. He also scored a run on Hal Morris's double in the third.
In Chicago, Scott Servais's two-run double snapped a fifth-inning tie as the Cubs scored a 9-5 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers before 38,593 fans -- the season's largest crowd at Wrigley Field.
Kevin Orie had three hits -- including a solo homer -- and scored three times for the Cubs. Jeff Cirillo doubled home two runs and Jeromy Burnitz added a solo homer for Milwaukee.
Steve Trachsel (4-5) got the win despite allowing five runs and nine hits. Scott Karl (2-8) was hammered for six runs and 10 hits in 4 1/3 innings.
In Houston, Matt Lawton hit a two-run homer in the first inning and Rich Robertson allowed one run over six innings as the Minnesota Twins beat the Astros 6-1.
Robertson (7-3) scattered six hits, walked two and struck out five for the win. Darryl Kile (7-3) took the loss.
The Twins added four runs in the eighth, sparked by Greg Myers's two-run double.
In St Louis, the Cardinals split a double header with the Cleveland Indians.
In the opener, Marquis Grissom's two-out RBI single in the eighth inning snapped a tie and triggered a five-run uprising as the Indians beat St Louis 8-3.
Julio Franco and Jim Thome had run-scoring hits in the eighth for the Indians and Sandy Alomar went 3-for-5 to extend his hitting streak to 15 games.
In the second game, Matt Morris allowed two runs and five hits in 8 1/3 innings and Ray Lankford doubled twice and drove in a run as the Cardinals got even with a 5-2 victory.
John Mabry added a solo homer for the Cards off Cleveland starter and loser Chad Ogea (5-6).
